claims.text: The initial cast MPEA has coarse grains larger than 10 µm.
Low configurational entropy or highly negative mixing enthalpy promotes brittle intermetallic formation in the as-cast alloy.
High configurational entropy in near-equimolar multi-principal-element compositions favors single-phase solid-solution stability.
Adding 0.5–2.0 at% C, N, or O can produce strong lattice distortion while remaining below the relevant interstitial solubility limit.
Severe plastic deformation of the interstitial-doped alloy will reduce its grain size below 50 nm.
Annealing at 900 °C for 3 minutes can stabilize an FCC-plus-HCP or FCC-plus-B2 dual-phase structure without significant grain growth or intermetallic formation.
Interstitial-induced lattice distortion and local chemical fluctuations increase the nucleation barrier for brittle intermetallic phases.
Interstitial additions promote metastable nanoscale HCP or B2 precipitates within a solid-solution matrix.
Interstitial elements suppress diffusion through a sluggish-diffusion effect.
Short annealing stabilizes the dual-phase structure through strain-induced phase transformation or spinodal decomposition.
Interstitial additions modify stacking-fault behavior and promote joint twinning and transformation-induced plasticity.
The proposed material will have hardness more than twice that of the cast baseline.
The proposed material will have yield strength more than twice that of the cast baseline.
The proposed material will retain more than 10% tensile elongation.
The proposed processing route will avoid brittle intermetallic formation.
The cast baseline has less than 5% tensile elongation.
Exceeding the interstitial solubility limit causes brittle carbide, nitride, or oxide precipitation.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration causes grain growth beyond 100 nm or intermetallic formation.
A base-alloy mixing enthalpy that is too negative prevents stabilization of the proposed solid solution.
Processing under argon prevents excessive oxidation during the proposed thermal treatment.
